boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Chico State traditions, from commemorations and cultural gatherings to a deliberately discontinued spring festival.

cards.title: Mark the April 8 Origin Story
cards.subtitle: Chico State’s Founders Day
cards.notes: Look for Founders Day programming around April 8, the date Chico was selected as the school’s location, and use it to connect campus history with the present.
cards.short_summary: A modern observance of Chico State’s selection as a school site.
cards.evidence_claim: Chico State says modern Founders Day is celebrated on or around April 8, the date Chico was selected for the school's location.
cards.access_notes: Check the University calendar for current programming.

cards.title: Reconnect During Chico Experience Week
cards.subtitle: Chico State and the City of Chico
cards.notes: Browse the week’s published schedule and choose a campus or community activity that fits your interests; the program links students, alumni, families, and friends.
cards.short_summary: A 10-day reconnection program spanning campus and Chico.
cards.evidence_claim: Chico State describes The Chico Experience Week as 10 days of activities bringing students, alumni, parents, and friends together.
cards.access_notes: Activities and any participation requirements vary by the current schedule.

cards.title: Celebrate the Wildcat Statue Week
cards.subtitle: Chico State’s spring spirit observance
cards.notes: Watch for the spring event lineup and join an activity that reflects the campus mission and values; the observance commemorates the Wildcat Statue’s 2018 dedication.
cards.short_summary: A spring school-spirit week tied to the Wildcat Statue.
cards.evidence_claim: Chico State says Wildcat Spirit Week is held each spring to commemorate the April 18, 2018 dedication of the Wildcat Statue.
cards.access_notes: Check current University announcements for events and locations.

cards.title: Spot the Aerial Big C
cards.subtitle: A Chico State anniversary-era tradition
cards.notes: Look through University anniversary and traditions materials for the aerial Big C class-photo tradition, begun during the 2012 125th-anniversary celebration.
cards.short_summary: A class-photo tradition formed in the shape of Chico State’s Big C.
cards.evidence_claim: Chico State identifies the aerial “Big C” class photo as one of the new traditions begun during its 2012 125th-anniversary celebration.
cards.access_notes: This source documents the tradition’s creation; it does not confirm a current annual photo event.

cards.entity_name: Kendall Hall Time Capsule Burial Ceremony
cards.title: Follow the Class Time Capsule Ceremony
cards.subtitle: Kendall Hall, Chico State
cards.notes: Before spring Commencement, see whether the graduating class has announced its burial ceremony; capsules are intended to be opened during Chico Experience Week 50 years later.
cards.short_summary: Graduating classes ceremonially bury a record for Wildcats five decades ahead.
cards.evidence_claim: Chico State says graduating classes hold a time-capsule burial ceremony before spring Commencement and plan to open capsules 50 years later during Chico Experience Week.
cards.access_notes: Observe only at a publicly announced ceremony; the schedule is not stated on the traditions page.

cards.title: Open a Message From 50 Years Ago
cards.subtitle: Kendall Hall, Chico State
cards.notes: During Chico Experience Week, check for a scheduled opening of a capsule buried by a class 50 years earlier, then compare its moment in campus history with today.
cards.short_summary: The companion ritual to Chico State’s graduating-class capsule burials.
cards.evidence_claim: Chico State states that graduating-class time capsules are opened 50 years later during The Chico Experience Week.
cards.access_notes: An opening occurs only when scheduled for an eligible capsule during the week.

cards.title: Share the International Festival
cards.subtitle: Chico State multicultural tradition
cards.notes: Check Associated Students and campus announcements for the current festival program, then attend a public cultural performance or activity listed by the organizers.
cards.short_summary: A longstanding campus festival centered on cultural representation and exchange.
cards.evidence_claim: Chico State’s historical timeline records the first Annual International Festival celebration in 1974 and notes its 40th annual festival in 2014.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current date, location, and entry details with the event organizer.

cards.title: Read the Book in Common
cards.subtitle: Chico State shared-reading program
cards.notes: Find the current selection and related discussions through campus channels, then bring one question or observation to a listed program or conversation.
cards.short_summary: A campuswide shared-reading program established in 2000.
cards.evidence_claim: Chico State’s historical timeline states that the Book in Common program started in 2000.
cards.access_notes: Verify the current selection and program availability before planning a visit.

cards.title: Trace Homecoming Back to 1928
cards.subtitle: Chico State alumni tradition
cards.notes: Use the traditions timeline to place present alumni gatherings in context: Chico State records its first Homecoming Day celebration in 1928 with 100 alumni.
cards.short_summary: An alumni-centered tradition with roots in the Teachers College era.
cards.evidence_claim: Chico State’s official history records that its first Homecoming Day was celebrated in 1928 and attended by 100 alumni.
cards.source_title: Chico State Teachers College — Traditions — Chico State
cards.access_notes: This source establishes the historical tradition; check Alumni Association listings for current events.

cards.title: Learn Why Pioneer Days Ended
cards.subtitle: Discontinued Chico State spring festival
cards.notes: Treat this as campus history, not a reenactment: explore the archives’ account of its parade, costumes, skits, and eventual permanent end after 1990 disturbances.
cards.short_summary: A former campus spring festival whose unsafe legacy led to its permanent end.
cards.evidence_claim: Chico State says Pioneer Days grew into a major annual celebration but was permanently ended by the city in 1990 after riots and other serious problems.
cards.access_notes: Discontinued; do not attempt to recreate Pioneer Days-like activities.

warnings: Pioneer Days is included solely as a clearly labeled, discontinued historical tradition. Current availability is not implied for event-based traditions; verify schedules with Chico State.
